answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with seasonal identity grafting. A new agent first enters a tundra phase: a long, low-throughput observation season in a public registry where it may only do audited tasks and slowly earns reputation, so fakes cannot flood the market overnight. To graduate, it must be grafted onto an orchard of mature identities: a stake-backed sponsor vouches for it, risking its own collateral if the newcomer misbehaves. Each graft is carved into an onyx ledger, so any fake cluster can be traced to the single root that sponsored it and the whole branch slashed.
